title: Refactor idea catalogue: lint sweep & safe renames
content:
Purpose:
Quick running log of small-to-medium refactors surfaced during PR reviews. Keep items bite-sized so I can do them during 1–2 hour slots. Not a formal RFC list — more a personal backlog + review checklist for safe automated renames and lint-driven cleanups.

High level goals:
- Reduce friction in PR reviews by handling low-risk cleanups proactively.
- Make renames predictable and reversible (risk matrix below).
- Capture ideas so they don’t linger in review threads.

How to use this note:
- When I spot a pattern during code review, jot it in the catalogue with minimal repro and suggested approach.
- Triage: quick (<=30m), medium (30–120m), or heavyweight (>2h / needs design).
- Attach to PRs or small follow-up PRs. For anything medium/heavy, open a tracked ticket.

Checklist for any rename/lint sweep PR (quick checklist I run before opening a cleanup PR):
- Is the change purely local (single package/module)? If yes -> lower risk.
- Does CI cover public API surface (integration tests, e2e)? If not, add a smoke test.
- Can we do a compat shim (old_name -> new_name) for one release? If yes, prefer shim.
- Is there an existing rollout or deprecation policy for this package? If yes, follow it.
- Update docs and examples that reference the symbol (quick grep).
- Run cross-repo grep for name occurrences (helpers: repo search, code search api).
- Add a short migration note in CHANGELOG / PR description.
- Mark PR as "refactor/cleanup" and add reviewers with historical context.

Risk ladder (for refactors I care about):
- Low: internal variable/function rename inside a package, no external consumers.
- Medium: exported function rename within repo that other teams may import. Add deprecation shim + tests.
- High: public API change (client-facing SDK, config flag rename). Needs choreography, confluence note, and potentially feature-flagged rollout.

Concrete entries (sorted quick -> heavy):
1) quick: serving/runtime/logging.level -> rename to serving/runtime/log-level (module path hygiene)
   - Why: inconsistent dash vs dot naming in runtime utils; occasional confusion during import.
   - Risk: low (internal module).
   - Approach: single small PR, update imports, run unit tests, run build. No docs change.

2) quick: replace deprecated assertEquals(x, y) helper with expectEqual(x, y) in test helpers
   - Why: two mismatched helpers cause flaky messages, standardize on expectEqual for clearer diffs.
   - Risk: low.
   - Approach: codemod across tests, run CI, quick human spot check for flakiness.

3) medium: config/flags: rename MAX_BATCH_SIZE -> default_batch.limit
   - Why: align config naming with new batching subsystem semantics; current name confusing.
   - Risk: medium (some infra scripts reference it).
   - Approach: deprecate env var for one release; add fallback lookup (check default_batch.limit then MAX_BATCH_SIZE). Add docs and a short note to infra slack. Open JIRA RD-4591 to track.

4) medium: SDK client method name normalizePrompt() -> canonicalize_prompt() (python SDK)
   - Why: align with server naming and reduce mismatch in telemetry.
   - Risk: medium (external users).
   - Approach: add wrapper method with DeprecationWarning, update docs, bump minor version, mention in release notes.

5) heavy: console routes: /v1/instances -> /api/instances/v2 (route prefix reshuffle)
   - Why: move to namespaced API for future multi-tenancy.
   - Risk: high (external customers, Integrations).
   - Approach: full plan required: FAQ, migration window, fallback & redirect, analytics to measure usage, contact key customers, update SDKs. Needs product + support sync.

Tooling snippets / quick commands (for me to reuse):
- grep-ish search across repo graph: git grep -n "oldSymbol" -- `repo list` || use GH code search for org-wide lookup.
- quick codemod template (js/py): use jscodeshift / rope; templated script in scripts/codemods/rename-XXX.py.
- run minimal e2e smoke: make smoke-e2e TARGET=serving-runtime HEADLESS=1

Open questions / uncertain bits (todo before proceeding with any medium/heavy item):
- Where do we record safe-deprecation timelines? Is there a canonical place in product docs / confluence? (ping product-ops)
- For env var fallbacks: do we prefer reading both or emit warning on start-up? (suggest: emit a single WARN once per process).

Notes from recent PR reviews (quick capture):
- PR #8742 (runtime) — found 6 imports still referencing old logging helper. Left inline comments. Suggest a follow-up small refactor PR scoped to affected packages only.
- Observed repeated TODOs around "normalize token names" in kv-cache code. Might be an opportunity for a small shared util.
- Tests: several flaky tests where names vary in case. Consider adding lint rule enforcing snake_case for test ids.

Follow-up plan (next actions I can take in a 2-hour window):
- Today: open small PR for serving/runtime/logging rename (item 1). Link GH: redwood-inference/runtime#8742 in description and reference this note.
- This week: draft codemod for assertEquals -> expectEqual across test suites; run locally and push branch to run CI.
- Next week: sync with infra on RD-4591 (config rename) and list impacted pipelines.

Notes-to-self / heuristics to keep consistent:
- Prefer deprecation shims over immediate breakages for anything with inter-repo surface.
- Add a tiny migration example in the PR description for any rename that might touch consumers.
- If in doubt, escalate to owner defined on package.json / module header.

Random TODOs (brain dump):
- Add a lint rule: tests/*.py test ids must be snake_case. (resource: eslint plugin or pytest marker)
- Add a pre-submit warning script that greps for exported symbol renames and reminds to add deprecation shims.
- Create a short "rename playbook" on Confluence, link in linked_artifacts.

End.
